_meta.note: V2 (2026-09-07): replaced the invented 'typical price range' / fairness verdict (likely_fair|somewhat_high|overpriced|cant_tell) with an audit of the quote actually supplied — new verdict enum (LOOKS_STRAIGHTFORWARD|NEEDS_CLARIFICATION|HARD_TO_COMPARE|SPECIFIC_CONCERNS_FOUND|NOT_ENOUGH_INFORMATION), quote_summary (extracted, not assumed), document_discrepancies (typed vs. uploaded document), arithmetic_check (only when actually calculable), specific_concerns (grounded only — missing info is NOT a red flag, it goes to unknowns_that_matter), second_quote.scope_comparable (a price alone isn't comparable), repair_vs_replace (no universal 50% rule, no age-only lifespan inference), what_to_say (not automatically a negotiation script), safety_note. Model changed from MODELS.SMART with an ad-hoc prompt to MODELS.SMART + router.outputGuard (v2 output standard) — this domain (reasoning about the visitor's own supplied situation) fits the generic v2 guard well, unlike PronounceItRight's specialist-knowledge domain. Verified live: all 5 cases pass, including both file-upload cases (image price discrepancy still caught; PDF pressure-tactic still surfaced as a grounded specific_concern with a genuine safety_note, not a remote diagnosis).

input.whatWentWrong: Not cooling properly, freezer is fine but the fridge side is warm
input.whatTheyToldYou: Technician said the compressor is failing and needs full replacement

output.understanding: Your 6-year-old Whirlpool refrigerator is cooling poorly on the fridge side while the freezer works fine, and a technician has diagnosed a failing compressor and quoted $450 for the replacement. No written breakdown of that $450 was provided.
output.verdict_explanation: The $450 figure is a single number with no visible breakdown into parts, labor, fees, or warranty terms. The diagnosis — a failing compressor — is a significant and specific claim for a symptom that can have more than one cause, so it is worth understanding what testing led there before approving a major repair. Without itemization, you also cannot tell what is and is not included in the price.

quote_summary.stated_diagnosis: Compressor is failing and needs full replacement

specific_concerns.concern: The $450 quote is a lump sum with no written itemization of parts, labor, fees, or warranty — nothing in what was provided shows how the number is composed.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: Without a breakdown you cannot verify what is included, compare meaningfully with another quote, or hold the provider to a specific scope if something goes wrong.

unknowns_that_matter: What diagnostic steps or tests were performed to confirm the compressor is the cause.
Whether the $450 covers parts, labor, and any fees together, or whether additional charges could be added later.
What warranty, if any, applies to the replacement compressor and to the labor.
Whether the replacement part would be OEM or aftermarket, which can affect longevity and any warranty.

repair_vs_replace.assessment: Whether to repair or replace depends on information not yet available — specifically the compressor replacement cost itemized separately from labor, and what a comparable replacement refrigerator would cost if you chose to buy new.
missing_information: Whether any warranty would apply to the repaired unit

questions_to_ask: Can you provide a written breakdown showing the cost of the compressor part separately from labor and any other fees?
What specific test or observation confirmed the compressor is the cause — I want to understand what was ruled out?
What warranty comes with the replacement compressor and with the labor?
Is the replacement compressor OEM or aftermarket?
output.what_to_say: Before I approve the work, I would like a written breakdown of the $450 — parts, labor, and any fees listed separately. I would also like to understand what diagnostic test confirmed the compressor is the problem, since I want to make sure I am approving the right repair. Can you provide those details?

second_opinion.reason: A compressor replacement is one of the more involved and costly refrigerator repairs, the diagnosis is a specific claim that rests on testing you have not yet seen documented, and you have no itemized quote to compare — a second opinion would let you verify both the diagnosis and the scope.

input.whatTheyToldYou: They said I need new brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels

output.understanding: You have a 2018 Honda Civic with 85,000 miles making a grinding noise when braking, and a shop has quoted you $1,800 to replace brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels. No written document was attached, so the only information available is what you typed.
output.verdict_explanation: The $1,800 quote covers a significant amount of work, but it was given as a single number with no breakdown of parts, labor, fees, or warranty. Without knowing how much of that $1,800 is parts versus labor, whether all four calipers are truly included or just some, and what diagnostic steps led to recommending caliper replacement specifically, there is not enough to evaluate whether this quote is reasonable or complete.

quote_summary.proposed_work: New brake pads, rotors, and calipers on all four wheels

specific_concerns.concern: All four calipers are included in the recommendation. No diagnostic basis for this was described.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: Replacing all four calipers adds meaningful cost to the job. You have no way to evaluate whether each replacement is warranted without knowing what was found during inspection.

unknowns_that_matter: No itemization exists: the split between parts cost and labor cost within the $1,800 is unknown, making it impossible to assess either component.
What diagnostic steps or inspection findings led to recommending caliper replacement on all four wheels rather than just pads and rotors is not stated.
Whether the quote includes OEM or aftermarket parts is not stated, and this can affect both cost and quality.
No warranty terms were mentioned, for either parts or labor.
Whether any fees such as shop supplies, disposal, or taxes are included in the $1,800 or would be added on top is unknown.
questions_to_ask: Can you break down the $1,800 into parts and labor separately, and list the cost for each component — pads, rotors, and calipers per axle or per wheel?
What specifically did you find on each caliper that leads you to recommend replacing all four?
Are the parts OEM, OEM-equivalent, or aftermarket, and what warranty comes with the parts and the labor?
Are there any additional fees — shop supplies, disposal, taxes — on top of the $1,800?
output.what_to_say: Before I approve this, I would like to see the quote broken down by parts and labor so I understand what each component costs. I also want to understand what you found on the calipers specifically, since replacing all four is a significant part of the total. Can you walk me through what the inspection showed and put the itemized breakdown in writing?

second_opinion.reason: The recommendation includes replacing all four calipers. Understanding what the shop found that supports this step will help you decide whether to proceed or get another look at the brakes.

output.safety_note: A grinding noise when braking can indicate brake wear severe enough to reduce stopping ability. Until the cause is confirmed and addressed, drive with extra following distance and avoid situations requiring hard braking if possible.

input.whatWentWrong: Reinigt nicht richtig, Geschirr kommt mit Essensresten heraus
input.whatTheyToldYou: Der Techniker sagte: "Die Umwälzpumpe ist defekt und muss komplett ersetzt werden"

output.understanding: Ihr etwa 4 Jahre alter Bosch Geschirrspüler reinigt nicht richtig, und ein Techniker hat die Umwälzpumpe als Ursache diagnostiziert und deren vollständigen Ersatz für 280 EUR angeboten. Über die genaue Aufschlüsselung dieses Betrags ist nichts bekannt.
output.verdict_explanation: Die 280 EUR sind eine Pauschalsumme ohne erkennbare Aufschlüsselung in Teilekosten, Arbeitszeit, Anfahrtsgebühr oder Diagnosekosten. Ohne diese Aufteilung lässt sich nicht beurteilen, was genau im Preis enthalten ist und ob etwaige Zusatzkosten noch hinzukommen. Außerdem ist nicht dokumentiert, welche Diagnose zur Entscheidung Umwälzpumpe geführt hat.
unknowns_that_matter: Wie setzt sich der Betrag von 280 EUR zusammen: Teilepreis, Arbeitszeit, Anfahrt, Diagnosegebühr?
Welche konkreten Tests oder Beobachtungen haben zur Diagnose der Umwälzpumpe geführt?
Gibt es eine Gewährleistung auf die Reparatur, und wenn ja, für wie lange und auf was genau?
Ist die Diagnosegebühr im Angebotspreis enthalten oder wird sie zusätzlich fällig, falls Sie die Reparatur ablehnen?

repair_vs_replace.assessment: Ohne den aktuellen Neupreis eines vergleichbaren Geräts und ohne Kenntnisse über den Allgemeinzustand des Geräts lässt sich nicht sinnvoll beantworten, ob Reparatur oder Neukauf die bessere Wahl ist.
missing_information: Aktueller Neupreis eines vergleichbaren Bosch Geschirrspülers
Allgemeiner Zustand und Reparaturhistorie des Geräts
Ob eine Herstellergewährleistung oder Händlergarantie noch läuft

questions_to_ask: Können Sie mir die 280 EUR aufschlüsseln: Was entfällt auf das Ersatzteil, was auf die Arbeitszeit, und sind Anfahrt und Diagnose bereits enthalten?
Wie haben Sie festgestellt, dass die Umwälzpumpe defekt ist und nicht zum Beispiel ein verstopfter Filter oder ein Problem mit den Sprüharmen?
Welche Gewährleistung gilt auf die ausgetauschte Pumpe und auf die Arbeitsleistung, und in welcher Form ist das schriftlich festgehalten?
Falls ich die Reparatur nicht beauftrage: Wird eine separate Diagnosegebühr fällig?
output.what_to_say: Vielen Dank für das Angebot. Bevor ich zustimme, hätte ich noch ein paar Fragen: Können Sie mir zeigen, wie sich die 280 EUR auf Teile, Arbeitszeit und eventuelle Anfahrtskosten aufteilen? Außerdem würde ich gerne verstehen, auf welcher Grundlage die Umwälzpumpe als Ursache identifiziert wurde. Und welche schriftliche Gewährleistung gilt auf die Reparatur?

second_opinion.reason: Der Betrag ist eine Pauschale ohne Aufschlüsselung und ohne dokumentierte Diagnoseverfahren. Eine zweite Einschätzung hilft Ihnen, die Diagnose zu überprüfen und die Kostenaufschlüsselung zu verstehen.

output.understanding: You have a 6-year-old Whirlpool refrigerator that isn't cooling properly, and ABC Appliance Repair has diagnosed a failed compressor and quoted you for a replacement. The document you uploaded shows more detail than the price you typed.
output.verdict_explanation: The document shows a total of $497.50, but you typed $450 — a $47.50 discrepancy that needs to be resolved before you approve anything. The itemization itself is reasonably clear (parts, labor hours, and a waived service call fee are all shown), so the main issue is confirming which total is actually being requested and understanding what diagnostic steps led to the compressor diagnosis.

quote_summary.labor: 2.5 hours at an unstated rate, totaling $187.50

arithmetic_check.assessment: The three line items on the document ($310.00 + $187.50 + $0.00) add up exactly to the $497.50 total shown on the document.

specific_concerns.concern: The total you typed ($450) does not match the document total ($497.50).
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: You may have been given a different verbal quote, or there may be a misunderstanding about what is included — this needs to be clarified in writing before you approve the work.

unknowns_that_matter: No warranty is stated anywhere on the document — neither on parts nor labor.
The labor rate per hour is not shown (only the total labor charge), so you cannot verify whether 2.5 hours at that rate is consistent with what was discussed.
No diagnostic steps are documented — it is worth understanding what testing or inspection led to the compressor diagnosis before authorizing a major component replacement.
Whether the compressor part is OEM or aftermarket is not stated, which can affect quality and any manufacturer warranty on the part itself.

repair_vs_replace.assessment: You don't have enough information yet to decide whether repair or replacement makes sense. To evaluate this, you would need to know the current cost of a comparable Whirlpool refrigerator and whether this unit has had prior repairs or reliability issues.
missing_information: Current replacement cost for a comparable Whirlpool refrigerator
Reliability history of this unit (any prior repairs or recurring issues)
Whether any other components are showing wear that might require additional repairs soon

questions_to_ask: The invoice shows $497.50 but I have $450 noted from our conversation — can you confirm which total applies and send me the correct written quote?
What testing or inspection confirmed the compressor is the cause, as opposed to another component?
Is the compressor part OEM or aftermarket, and does it carry any parts warranty?
Is there a labor warranty, and if so, for how long?
output.what_to_say: I want to move forward but I need to sort out a discrepancy first — the invoice shows $497.50 and I have $450 from our earlier conversation, so can you confirm the correct total in writing? I also want to understand what diagnostic steps confirmed the compressor is the issue before I approve the replacement, and whether there is any warranty on the parts and labor.

second_opinion.reason: The quote does not document what diagnostic steps were used to reach the compressor diagnosis. A second opinion would let you confirm whether that diagnosis is correct before committing to a major component replacement.

output.understanding: You have an estimate for a 2018 Honda Civic with a grinding noise when braking. The quote totals $1,708 and includes replacement of brake pads and rotors on all four corners, plus all four calipers and 4.5 hours of labor.
output.verdict_explanation: The arithmetic checks out: the seven line items sum to exactly $1,708.00. Two concrete concerns are present. First, the quote recommends replacing all four calipers at $660 total with no documented inspection finding in the written estimate to explain why — calipers are not routine in a standard brake service. Second, the estimate includes a 24-hour approval deadline, which limits your time to ask follow-up questions or get a second opinion. The written estimate also contains no warranty language covering parts or labor.

quote_summary.stated_diagnosis: Grinding noise when braking — no further diagnostic finding stated in the document
quote_summary.proposed_work: Replace front brake pads, front brake rotors (2), rear brake pads, rear brake rotors (2), front calipers (2), and rear calipers (2); labor 4.5 hours

arithmetic_check.assessment: The seven line items ($89 + $180 + $79 + $160 + $340 + $320 + $540) sum to exactly $1,708.00, matching the stated total.

specific_concerns.concern: All four calipers are included in the quote with no documented reason. The written estimate states only a grinding noise — it does not describe any caliper-specific finding (seized piston, uneven wear, fluid leak, etc.) that would support replacing $660 worth of calipers.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: Calipers are not a routine part of a brake job; recommending all four without a documented reason is worth understanding before you approve, since it is the single largest parts line on the quote.

specific_concerns.concern: The estimate includes a 24-hour approval deadline to lock in the price.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: A tight deadline limits your ability to ask follow-up questions, get a second opinion, or simply think it over — which matters more when the quote includes components beyond a standard brake service.

specific_concerns.concern: No warranty of any kind is stated on the written estimate.
specific_concerns.why_it_matters: With $1,708 in work and six new components, having nothing in writing about parts or labor coverage leaves you unprotected if something fails shortly after the repair.

unknowns_that_matter: What specific inspection finding led to recommending all four calipers — no diagnostic note appears in the written estimate.
Whether the parts are OEM, OEM-equivalent, or aftermarket — this affects quality and price comparisons.
Whether a diagnostic fee was charged and whether it is included in or separate from the quoted total.
Whether there is any warranty on parts or labor, and if so, what it covers and for how long.
questions_to_ask: What specific condition did you find on the calipers that makes replacing all four necessary — can you show me or describe what you saw?
Are the parts OEM, OEM-equivalent, or aftermarket?
What warranty do you provide on parts and labor for this repair, and can you put that in writing on the estimate?
Is the 24-hour deadline firm, or can I have until tomorrow afternoon — I want to make sure I understand the scope before I approve?
output.what_to_say: I want to approve this, but I have a few questions before I do. The caliper replacement is the part I am least clear on — can you walk me through what you found that makes replacing all four necessary? I would also like to know what warranty comes with the work, and whether you can add that to the written estimate. Once I have those answers I can move quickly.

second_opinion.reason: The caliper recommendation adds $660 to what would otherwise be a straightforward brake job, and the written estimate provides no documented finding to support it — a second shop can tell you whether their inspection agrees with that diagnosis.

output.safety_note: A grinding noise when braking warrants prompt inspection and diagnosis. Until you have had the brakes evaluated and repaired, avoid highway speeds and situations requiring hard stops.
